In the Supreme Court of the United States 

No. 16-1094 

REPUBLIC OF SUDAN, PETITIONER 

v. 

RICK HARRISON, ET AL. 

ON PETITION FOR A WRIT OF CERTIORARI 
TO THE UNITED STATES COURT OF APPEALS 
FOR THE SECOND CIRCUIT 

SUPPLEMENTAL BRIEF FOR THE RESPONDENTS 

On January 19, 2018, the Fourth Circuit issued its de-
cision in Kumar v. Republic of Sudan, 880 F.3d 144.  That 
decision  addresses  service  of  process  on  Sudan,  by  the 
same  means  used  here,  in  another  suit  arising  from  the 
U.S.S. Cole bombing.  The Fourth Circuit held that deliv-
ering  a  service  packet  addressed  to  Sudan’s  minister  of 
foreign  affairs  at  the  Sudanese  embassy  in  Washington 
does  not  comport  with  the  requirements  of  28  U.S.C. 
1608(a)(3).  Id. at 158.  In so doing, it recognized that “[its] 
holding conflicts” with the Second Circuit’s holding in this 
case.  Id. at 159. 

In  light  of  the  resulting  circuit  conflict,  the  Kumar 
plaintiffs, who are represented by the same counsel as re-
spondents here, are simultaneously filing a petition for a 

(1)

2 

writ  of  certiorari.    The  petition  asks  the  Court  to  grant 
review  in  Kumar  and  further  suggests  that  the  Court 
should either grant this petition or hold it pending the dis-
position of Kumar.  Respondents refer the Court to the 
petition in Kumar and respectfully request that it be con-
sidered together with this petition. 

Respectfully submitted.
